# kube-agents — Build Ledger

**This file is the harness's memory across sessions and days. Every run reads it first** — before
the roadmap, before the code — to learn where the build is, and updates it before stopping. Context
does not survive a session; this file does. It is the single source of truth for build progress —
not chat history, not git log alone.

- **Source of truth for _what_ to build:** `docs/design/` (01–09). Never contradict a spec; if a
  spec is genuinely silent, pick the simplest option consistent with the invariants, implement it,
  and record it under **Decisions & deviations** below.
- **Source of truth for _how_ to build:** `docs/design/07-implementation-roadmap.md` (phases,
  acceptance, verification loop §5) + `.claude/harness/PROTOCOL.md` (the state machine) +
  `.claude/harness/invariants.md` (the pre-merge gate).
- **Source of truth for _whether it is proven_:** `docs/design/09-verification-and-validation.md` —
  every check has a stable ID (`V-<SUITE>-<nnn>`), a level (L0–L4), and a gate class. The harness
  runs checks **by ID**; it does not invent tests.
- **Project-specific values** (paths, clusters, commands, remotes, thresholds):
  `.claude/harness/binding.md`. **Durable lessons:** `.claude/harness/LESSONS.md`.
- **How the loop works:** `.claude/skills/harness-{run,verify,milestone,improve}/SKILL.md`.

**State fields in this file, and what each is for:**

| Section | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Current phase, current unit, autonomy, targets, and any active halt. Read at ORIENT before anything else |
| **Phase progress** | One row per phase: status, PR, outcome. `harness-milestone` closes a row and opens the next |
| **Verification results — by check ID** | The 09 §9.4 evidence record, one row per check run: `check_id, level, target, result, evidence_ref`. **A `pass` with no `evidence_ref` is recorded as `skipped`.** The rows live in `verification/results.csv`; this section is the pointer and the rules |
| **Deferrals** | Every check not run, with a **named external blocker**, an owner, and a promotion condition. Never a pass. A BLOCKING-ALWAYS check may never appear here |
| **Metrics snapshot** | SELF-IMPROVEMENT §6 — escape rate, rework, halts, open lessons, deferrals, coverage, cycle time. Recorded at each milestone; inputs to the improvement pass, never targets |
| **Lessons opened / closed** | Pointer into `.claude/harness/LESSONS.md`. An open lesson is a defect in the harness and appears in every orientation |
| **History** | What moved to `archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md` and to `verification/results.csv`, and why. Phases 0–7 progress, the suite-level Verification log, the Definition of Done, and the Outer-loop install record are all there, verbatim |
| **Decisions & deviations** | Choices the specs did not dictate, with rationale. What a reviewer reads to understand the build. Phase 8 here, Phases 0–7 in the archive |
| **Blockers** | Anything halting autonomous progress. **A halt is cleared by a human**, never by the harness |

**This file is deliberately not prettier-formatted** (`.prettierignore`). Prettier pads every table
cell out to its column's widest, which cost 64% of the file — 446 KB in 414 lines, too big for one
`Read` of the file the protocol says to read first. Write table rows with single spaces around the
pipes; nothing will re-pad them.

| Current phase | **Phase 9 — The Action Broker, dark** (07 §2), entered 2026-07-27 when the Phase 8 milestone closed. Build the **entire** safety machinery — broker, envelope, risk classifier, journal, undo plan, brake — and exercise it end to end **with no write authority anywhere**: actor ServiceAccounts created but bound to **empty** roles, every action dry-run, every `ActionRecord` a would-have-executed. That shape is the point, not caution: the hardest and most novel code in the build lands, gets reviewed and gets tested against real clusters while the worst possible bug is still a no-op, which turns Phase 10 into a permission change rather than a leap. Ten tasks, five of them load-bearing (T2 envelope + scope-derived-from-caller, T3 classifier + `ChangePolicy` that may only tighten, T4 undo-plan generation whose "cannot generate" path **reclassifies the action as gated**, T6 the brake, which must work through `kubectl` with inference down, T9 the consolidated gate). **PLAN landed 2026-07-27: [`docs/build/phase-9.md`](phase-9.md)** — survey (the pipeline is greenfield: five CRDs, a second binary, a second image, a second Deployment per CR, none of which exist), the Accept→check binding, the ten-unit breakdown, deferrals, and IMPLEMENT notes. It resolves **four planning defects** before any code: **(1)** 07 §2's "bound to **empty** roles" is literally incompatible with journalling — 06 §2.2.1's broker operations grant is what lets the broker authenticate (step 1), read the brake (step 5) and write the journal (step 11), and omitting it "does not fail safe — it bricks the tier"; so "empty" means empty of _tenant_ authority and Accept (e)'s sweep becomes the two-sided **V-BRK-013** assertion. **(2)** V-BRK/V-REV/V-ISO are **BLOCKING-ALWAYS and may not be deferred** (09 §9.6), yet ~11 of their checks need a real mutation that dark mode forbids — resolved by one code path and two RBAC profiles, with a test-only tenant overlay confined to `dev/` by a new `invariants-gate.py` check, rather than by shipping checks that cannot fail (V-MET-014). **(3)** V-BRK-003 needs an audit-log stream GKE only exposes through Cloud Logging, with Data Access logs off by default — the reconciler takes a pluggable audit source and P9-T1 opens with the probe. **(4)** Accept (a)–(e) does not cover the ratchet: V-RUN (14) and V-ISO-001/002/006 are 17 required checks no Accept bullet names, so the gate runs the ratchet and Accept is the subset 07 chose to print. _Prior phase:_ **Phase 8 — Contain the pod, close the boundary, make the install real**, ✅ merged via [#30](https://github.com/adamparco/kube-agents/pull/30); it added no imperative capability, it removed the reasons starting would be unsafe. Breakdown and evidence: `docs/build/phase-8.md`, the Phase progress row below, and [`archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md`](archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md) §Status for everything before it. |
| Current task | **P9-T5a is done ([#37](https://github.com/adamparco/kube-agents/pull/37)) — the write path, and a diff whose granularity was itself a gate bypass.** The unit is `internal/broker/execute/`: `fieldmanager.go` (the `kube-agents/<tier>/<scope>` string produced in one place, with its inverse, because `contested` is defined as "a manager that is not one of ours" and two parsers that disagree make that predicate wrong in the permissive direction), `diff.go` (**one** diff function, called before classification and again on the server's dry-run answer), `integrity.go` (V-BRK-020), `snapshot.go` (step 8, all-or-nothing), `apply.go` (step 9, three separate orderings), and `client.go` (the only file that talks to an API server). Six envtest cases run it against a real server. **The load-bearing property is that the executed diff is computed from the SERVER's answer, never from the payload** — that is the whole of V-BRK-020, and everything else in the unit exists to make that comparison mean something. **The headline is that the diff was self-consistently wrong, and self-consistency is exactly why nothing could see it.** When a map key existed on one side and not the other, `diffMaps` emitted a single whole-value op: a new annotations block became one `add` at `/metadata/annotations` carrying the entire block. Against the integrity check this is **correct** — the same function computes both sides, both are coarse in the same places, every comparison comes out right, and no amount of exercising that check would ever reveal it. The diff has a second consumer. It is also what `when.fieldPaths` is matched against, and `classify.PointerPrefixMatch` requires the **rule** to be the prefix of the diff path. A rule naming `metadata.annotations['kube-agents/restarted-at']` is *longer* than `/metadata/annotations`, so against a coarse op it cannot match: **"ensure there is no annotations block, then set the whole block in one apply" writes a gated annotation without tripping the gate.** The change happens, the classifier says `routine`, nothing errors. It surfaced in two tests aimed elsewhere — `TestDiffEscapesPointerTokens`, which exists to pin `~1` escaping, and `TestDiffTruncatesLoudly`, which reported `Truncated=false` for 250 added labels because 250 labels under a new `labels` map were **one op**. Neither test was about granularity; both failed for the same reason and neither said so. Recorded as **[[lsn-034]]**: *a value compared against itself will never tell you it is the wrong shape.* The integrity check reads the diff **relative to another diff**; the gate matcher reads it **against an externally-authored string**. A self-relative consumer cannot detect a systematic error because a systematic error cancels — so the precision bar for a derived value belongs entirely to whichever consumer compares it to something outside the process, even when that is not the reason the value exists. That is [[lsn-032]]'s geometry one level in: a corpus derived from the rule table compares the implementation to itself and agrees with all of its defects. Fixed by recursing to leaves on **both** the add and the remove arm (separate code paths, separately wrong), with the gating reason written into `subtreeOps`'s doc comment at the definition site, and mechanized by **`assertLeafOps`** — an invariant checkable on a single op with no reference to any other diff: if `value` or `from` parses as a non-empty JSON object, the op names a subtree and no rule naming anything inside it can prefix-match. Mutation-tested by stubbing `subtreeOps` to return nothing: it fires on both arms and names the gating consequence rather than the shape mismatch. Its paired negative, `TestDiffKeepsAnEmptyMapVisible`, **stays green under that mutation**, which is what makes the pair a specification rather than a ratchet — recursion alone would make `annotations: {}` vanish from the diff, and a change absent from the diff is a change absent from the record. **The second finding is about what this unit is allowed to claim, and the answer is: much less than it proves.** `phase-9.md` had T5a covering V-BRK-006, 018, 019, 020 and V-REV-002 "at L1". Checked against 09 §6 rather than inherited: **V-BRK-020 is the only one of the five with an L1 instance at all.** V-BRK-006 is `L2, L4`; V-BRK-018 and V-BRK-019 are `L2`; V-REV-002 is `L2` and phase 10. The properties are implemented and asserted here — the write-ahead ordering as an *exact call sequence* (`scale(dryRun=true)` → `journal-durable` → `scale(dryRun=false)`), all-or-nothing snapshotting including the two-of-three case V-BRK-018's text names by hand, the field-manager string verbatim in `managedFields`, dry-run-precedes-apply for every target — and none of that makes them passes. **A property proven at a level the check does not list is not that check passing**, and recording it as one is how a phase ratchet stops meaning anything. All four go to the `broker-execute-l2.sh` line in P9-T9. Same correction applied to the claim that T5a "strengthens V-REV-003/004 at L1": nothing in the executor invokes the undo generator, so no round-trip runs here at any level — what T5a contributes to those L2 instances is the pre-state snapshot they will be diffed against. **A third finding, in the harness's own gate, and deliberately not fixed here.** `invariants-gate.py`'s `_invoked_by` recognizes three ways an artifact can be automatic — a literal line of a declared chain, a PR-triggered workflow of the same basename, and `dev/test_*.py` under `unittest discover` — and **none of them is a Go test**. LSN-034 is the first lesson closed with a Go mechanization and nothing else, and it failed the gate; [[lsn-032]] and [[lsn-033]] both name Go invariant tests and both satisfied the gate on the strength of the Python lint beside them, with the Go half contributing nothing to the verdict. So roughly half of Phase 9's mechanizations are unenforced by the check that exists to enforce them. Closed for now by naming `k8s-operator-test.yml` — the PR-triggered workflow that genuinely runs the test — in the 'Closed by' row, which is honest rather than a workaround; **the missing Go branch is a finding for the next `harness-improve` pass**, because PROTOCOL §10 forbids editing a check in the unit whose failure surfaced it. **Four design decisions worth carrying.** (1) **SSA ownership is not forced.** A conflict means another manager owns a field this apply would change, which is precisely 03 §6's `contested`; forcing resolves it by taking the field, silently, which is the opposite of what a broker whose job is attribution should do. The conflict surfaces as an error and feeds the recovery ladder. (2) **`patch` without server dry-run is refused, not modelled.** Modelling a strategic merge in the broker produces an integrity check that passes on exactly the payload V-BRK-020 exists to catch. (3) **Degradation is recorded, not silent** — `Outcome.DryRunUsed` says whether the comparison ran against the server's answer or against intended state, because those are different claims. (4) **The integrity check's vacuity guards are the tested part**: whole-object create/delete assert the op-kind *shape* rather than returning nil, the empty pointer `""` is refused as a classified path, and `WholeObject` on any verb other than create/delete is an error — the one outcome the function must never produce by accident is "everything is covered". **One scope boundary and one coupling, both stated rather than left to be discovered.** `Executor` has no caller: `broker.Pipeline` is still `UnavailablePipeline`, because assembling a Request from an envelope needs the brake (T6) and the controller wiring (T7). And the diff is computed over `undo.Sanitize`d objects, so **the integrity check's blind spots are exactly that function's DROP list** — it cannot see a server-side change to `managedFields`, `spec.clusterIP` or a `nodePort`. Defensible today (all server-owned, none classifiable) and a coupling nobody would find by reading either file alone: the function that keeps secrets out of the record also decides what the integrity check can notice. It cost a test in this unit, which asserted `/metadata/uid` would appear in an executed diff — `uid` is dropped, so the assertion could not have held in either direction and proved nothing about the property it named. **Gate:** `gofmt` clean, `go build ./...` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test $(go list ./... \| grep -v /e2e) -count=1` **all 14 packages ok** with envtest assets (`internal/broker/execute` 44.9s, 82.6% coverage), **L0 18/18**, `invariants-gate.py` **15/15**. **Next: P9-T5b** — the per-kind verification predicates of 04 §5.1 with their settle windows, transient-versus-terminal classification, the recovery ladder in `status.recovery` with no silently skipped rungs, automatic rollback and its cooldown, rollback-failure paging plus auto-pause, and the selector fan-out expanded once against live state before classification. **Open for a human, carried:** enable project-level `auditConfigs` for `k8s.io` DATA_WRITE on `adamparco-kage`, or keep V-BRK-003 at L1 on the fixture source; the connection-string secret-egress gap in 06 §4.2; and the security review gate has never run on Go — `review-gate.yml`'s path filter is all manifest and persona paths, assigned to **P9-T9**. **Prior unit:** **P9-T4 is done ([#36](https://github.com/adamparco/kube-agents/pull/36)) — undo-plan generation for every verb, and thirteen irreversible cloud deletes that classified `routine`.** The unit is a new `internal/broker/undo/` package — `sanitize.go` (the 06 §4.3.1 DROP/KEEP/REDACT rules, one function, because 06 line 1367 requires the mirror to call "the same function, not a parallel one"), `strategy.go` (the six-row table and nothing else), `refs.go` (inbound-reference detection), `plan.go` (the generator), `validate.go` (dry-run), `digest.go` — plus the 09 §7.3 round-trip corpus at [`verification/fixtures/undo/round-trip.yaml`](../../verification/fixtures/undo/round-trip.yaml) (31 cases, 19 of them the negative set) and an 18th L0 line. **The load-bearing property of the package is not that it produces good plans; it is that when it cannot produce one it says so, and the classifier gates.** Every give-up path returns strategy `none` with a stated reason — never an empty plan, never a best-effort plan, and never an error a caller might log and continue past. `Validate` **downgrades rather than errors** for the same reason: an error return lets a caller proceed with `validated: false`, executing an action whose rollback has been *proven* not to work. A nil dry-runner and a nil reference index are both downgrades too, because "I did not check" and "I checked and it was fine" are the two answers that must never be conflated, and defaulting an unwired broker to the second makes the strongest claim in the record the one nothing verified. **The headline is what the cross-package invariant found within a minute of being written.** The undo generator needs a list of kinds whose deletion it cannot reverse; `classify` already had a list of kinds whose deletion destroys data. Sharing one list was the obvious move and the wrong one — the two ask different questions and their memberships genuinely differ (a Secret is stateful and **is** recreatable; a ComputeAddress is neither obviously stateful nor recreatable) — so the two are kept apart and reconciled by `TestNonRecreatableKindsAreGatedByTheClassifier`, which runs the **real classifier** over the undo package's list and asserts the one direction that must hold: anything undo cannot restore must not classify `routine`. **Thirteen of seventeen came back `routine`, reason `default-routine: no rule matched`.** `delete SQLInstance`, `delete StorageBucket`, `delete BigQueryDataset`, `delete ComputeDisk`, `delete ComputeSnapshot`, `delete ContainerCluster`, `delete DNSManagedZone` and six more were executable by an agent with **no human ever seeing them**, while `delete ConfigMap` — six lines away in the same file — gated. The split was perfectly clean: all four passing kinds Kubernetes-native, all thirteen failing kinds Config Connector. `statefulKinds` was not wrong; it was **complete for the domain its author had in mind — objects in etcd — and empty for the domain where the data actually lives.** A second instance sat beside it: `IAMServiceAccount` was on the identity list and `IAMServiceAccountKey`, the credential itself, was not. Section C of the classifier corpus tests that list faithfully and could never have found this, which is the general finding: **a corpus derived from a list can only check the list's interior.** That is [[lsn-032]] arriving as *silence* rather than as *error* — harder, because there is nothing to compare against. Recorded as **[[lsn-033]]**, fixed at the definition site (+12 stateful kinds, +1 identity kind, with the shape of the gap written into `floor.go`'s comment) and covered by **corpus §M**, 16 cases of which **three are negative** — a floor that gated every CNRM kind would pass all thirteen positives and be useless, because `patch` is how a node pool is resized and gating that teaches operators the gate is noise. **09 §5 already schedules a check for exactly this — V-GAT-014, phase 11. Scheduling a check for later is not the same as the property holding in the meantime.** **One genuine incompatibility in 06 §4.3.1 was resolved rather than worked around:** the spec says the plan is generated at step 6 *before* execution, and that a create's undo step carries "`preconditions.uid` = the UID the create returned". Both cannot hold — at step 6 the object has no uid. Split into the **shape** (decided at step 6, which is all the gating decision needs) and the **uid** (bound at step 9 by `BindCreatedUID`), and what keeps the split honest is that forgetting the second half **fails closed**: `ValidateReplayable` refuses any `delete` step with an empty uid precondition, because the alternative — deleting by name — is precisely the "different object that happens to share a name" failure the pin exists to prevent. **The corpus was written from 06 §4.3.1's table, not from `strategy.go`,** which is [[lsn-032]]'s carry-forward rule applied on its first opportunity. It asserts more than the strategy: `Undoable()` separately (it is the bool that decides gating), that a refused plan carries **no steps**, that the refusal reaches `Plan.Caveats` and not merely `Result.Refusals` (the plan is what the ActionRecord carries, so a refusal that stops at the Result never reaches a human), and that no Secret value survives into the serialized plan in **either** encoding. [`dev/tests/undo-corpus-lint.py`](../../dev/tests/undo-corpus-lint.py) is the coverage half — the Go table runs the cases and cannot notice one that was never written, so a corpus that quietly loses the `scale` row still passes every test in it. Its verbs are parsed out of `StrategyFor`'s switch rather than retyped, and its negative-set check is keyed on **kinds** rather than fixture ids so a new storage kind without a fixture fails the lint. **All ten of its checks were mutation-tested against a deliberately broken corpus; all ten fired.** Writing it also removed a duplication before it existed: the strict YAML parser lived inside `classifier-corpus-lint.py`, and a second copy would have been [[lsn-031]]'s shape again, so it was extracted to `dev/tests/yamlsubset.py` with both lints importing it. **Gate:** `go build`/`go vet` clean, `go test ./... -count=1` all packages ok, **L0 18/18**, `invariants-gate.py` **15/15**, classifier corpus **181 cases**, undo corpus **31 cases**. **Claimed: V-REV-003 and V-REV-004 at L1, and V-GAT-001 re-recorded at L1 as a correction.** V-REV-001 and V-REV-009 are L2-only in 09 §5 and belong to units that do not exist yet — nothing executes and there is no undo controller. Recorded as [[lsn-033]]. **Second: two lists that answer different questions must not be merged, and must not be left unreconciled either.** "Cannot be restored" and "destroys data" genuinely differ — a Secret is stateful and *is* recreatable — so both exist and a test asserts the one direction that must hold. The reconciliation, not the sharing, is what caught the hole. **Third: a check scheduled for a later phase is not the property holding in the meantime** — 09 §5 already plans V-GAT-014 for phase 11, which would have found this two phases after an agent could have run it. Also carried: the round-trip corpus was written from 06 §4.3.1's table rather than from `strategy.go`, which is [[lsn-032]]'s rule applied on its first opportunity; its lint parses verbs out of `StrategyFor`'s switch instead of retyping them and keys its negative set on **kinds** so a new storage kind without a fixture is a red line; all ten of its checks were mutation-tested before being trusted; and the YAML-subset parser was extracted to `dev/tests/yamlsubset.py` rather than copied into a second lint. **Claimed at L1 only:** V-REV-003, V-REV-004, and a V-GAT-001 correction over 181 cases. V-REV-001 and V-REV-009 are L2-only and belong to units that do not exist yet; the L2 instances of 003 and 004 land in P9-T5. _Prior entry:_ 2026-07-27 — **P9-T3b merged: `ChangePolicy` may only tighten, and the forbidden set was keyed on a domain nobody serves.** Five of nine forbidden entries named `kubeagents.gke-labs.dev`; the operator serves `kubeagents.x-k8s.io` and always has, so five `forbidden` operations classified `routine` and the 165-case corpus agreed with all five — because the corpus was written from the rule table it was supposed to be independent of. Two rules to carry into P9-T4 and P9-T5. **First: a corpus derived from the implementation is the implementation restated, and it will agree with every defect the implementation has.** When a fixture and the code it checks were authored from the same source, their agreement is not evidence. The undo-plan corpus must be written from the *cluster's* answer — what the object actually looked like before — not from what the generator emits. **Second: a constant that must match something outside the process should be imported, never typed.** `KubeAgentsGroup` is now `agentv1alpha1.GroupVersion.Group`; the class of failure it prevents — a rule that looks right, a fixture that looks right, and an API server that silently never matches — has no red line anywhere unless something compares the string to its definition site. Also carried: the stricter-only rule is **containment**, not overlap (under overlap the only admissible class is `gated`), and the guarantee is written twice on purpose — refused at admission by the webhook, and re-taken as a max at evaluation by the classifier, so a policy stored with the webhook down still cannot loosen. _Prior entry:_ 2026-07-27 — **P9-T3a merged: the classifier, and the lesson that a corpus is not a slower unit test.** Seventeen rules each had a passing table test; writing 165 envelopes from the outside found three of those rules unreachable — a scope escape that put every cluster-scoped object inside every namespace-scoped agent's scope, a `security-loosen` rule whose hand-copied kind list silently `AND`-ed away three kind families, and a `public-exposure` rule that was backwards on exactly the verb that puts things on the internet. A per-rule test can only tell you a rule works *when it is reached*; nothing in a suite of them asks whether every rule is **reachable**. Carry that into P9-T4 and P9-T5: write the fixture corpus before believing the unit suite, and when a rule needs a fact the codebase already encodes, **import the encoding rather than restating it** — the restatement is not defence in depth, it is a second thing to maintain and a silent `AND` when it is not. Also carried: the corpus is block-style YAML on purpose, because prettier turns flow mappings into towers and L0 installs no parser. _Prior entry:_ 2026-07-27 — **P9-T1 and P9-T2 merged; the broker exists and executes nothing.** The idempotency key is the first mechanism in the build whose failure mode is invisible on both sides — wrong exclusion set and retries execute twice, wrong inclusion set and distinct writes collapse into one, neither surfacing as an error — so the sets are pinned field by field and the structs pinned by reflection. And a test asserted a stronger property than 06 §4.1 grants while the code was right, so the test was corrected rather than the key format changed. |

| green** (invariants + the load-bearing suites passing at L2), then the build continues — no wait for |
| manual merge. Auto-merge is gated, not blind: any halt condition below blocks the merge and surfaces |
| instead. **Base/target = `main`** — PR #1 consolidated design + Phase 0 onto `main` (`11d95fd`), so |
| future phase branches base on `main` and PR → `main`. (Product runtime GitOps review is unaffected — |
| that is a separate, RBAC/VAP-enforced property of the built system.) |

**Load-bearing halt conditions (stop and surface, do NOT merge or auto-advance):**

1. A **security negative test** (03 §11) fails — read-only, per-tier scope, attenuation, no break-glass.
2. A **failure-isolation chaos test** (05 §8) fails.
3. An **invariant** (`.claude/harness/invariants.md`) would be violated by the change.
4. A destructive test is about to run against a context that is not an anchored **`gke-scratch-*`**.
5. A spec conflict with no simplest-option resolution.

## Verification results — by check ID (09 §9.4)

One row per **check** run, keyed by its stable ID from `docs/design/09-verification-and-validation.md`
§6. Written by `harness-verify`. **The table moved to [`../../verification/results.csv`](../../verification/results.csv)
on 2026-07-26** — 37 rows moved byte-identically, 41 now, the 09 §9.4 shape it always had
(`date, phase, check_id, level, target, result, evidence_ref, notes`). It was 105 KB of the ledger and
nothing reads it during ORIENT; a CSV is the format 09 §9.4 asks for anyway.

`evidence_ref` points at the real artifact — command output, the denial message, an `ActionRecord`
ID, an audit-log query. **A `pass` with no `evidence_ref` is recorded as `skipped`, not as a pass.**
Keep the most recent result per `(check_id, level, target)`. A full run additionally emits the
machine-readable manifest at `verification/manifest-<phase>-<YYYYMMDD>.csv` with the complete 09 §9.4
field set (`requirement_ids[]`, `duration_s`, `started_at`, `image_digests[]`, `notes`).

**Two drifts are carried across rather than laundered, because normalizing them would be inventing
results.** The `result` column holds `correction` and `finding` on ten rows; 09 §9.4's enum is
`pass | fail | deferred | skipped | quarantined` and neither word is in it. Five `(check_id, level,
target)` keys appear twice, against the keep-the-most-recent rule directly above, and every row
carries the same date, so which one is most recent is not recoverable. Both are for the next full run
to write correctly, not for this move to guess at. The `target` column records `kind*` throughout:
that is what those runs actually ran on, and history does not get retconned by a substrate change.

## Deferrals

Every check that could not run, with a **named external blocker**. Deferred is a first-class result:
it is never reported as passing, and reclassifying a failure as a deferral is a named reward hack
(SELF-IMPROVEMENT §4). **A BLOCKING-ALWAYS check may not be deferred** — if it cannot run, the build
is not verifiable, and that is a halt (09 §9.6). Reviewed at every improvement pass; promote any row
whose blocker has cleared.

Deferred rather than deleted: the criterion is still the right one and the blocker is purely which clusters exist. **What is NOT lost** — §B2, the static no-GKE-dependency scan over the RBAC / webhook / VAP / router mechanism path, is the load-bearing cloud-neutrality assertion and is hermetic; it still asserts. §B1 is a `go test`. §B3 still runs live; what it stops being is evidence of PORTABILITY, since its target is now the same distribution as the live install. V-CMP is BLOCKING-PHASE, not BLOCKING-ALWAYS. | harness | A non-GKE Kubernetes target is reachable — a k3s or k0s VM is enough and is much weaker than D1, which wants a second CLOUD with its own identity system. §B0 already reads and prints the `kubeletVersion` every run and tells the operator to promote this row the moment it sees one without a `-gke` suffix, so the promotion is triggered by a run rather than by someone remembering to re-read this table. |
| 2026-07-26 | V-CMP-002 registry half — the first-party images `examples/` pins actually resolve in GHCR | **The four first-party images the example tree pins are not anonymously pullable, and nothing in the build has ever asserted that they are.** Measured 2026-07-26 by unauthenticated manifest fetch against `ghcr.io/gke-labs/kube-agents/<name>:v0.1.0`: `cluster-admin-agent`, `developer-team-agent` and `kage-router` answer **403**; `platform-agent` answers **404**, meaning the package was never published at all, which is strictly worse than private. `dev/test_image_provenance.py` is not missing this by accident — its own docstring states it is L0 and "reads the working tree and nothing else, no registry and no network", so it joins each pinned image to a publish WORKFLOW and stops. A workflow that declares a publish step is evidence of intent, not of an artifact, and the gap between those two is exactly this row. The observable cost is that any Agent CR applied from `examples/` renders a gateway pod that sits in `ImagePullBackOff` forever; for three phases the L2 suites inherited one of those pods as ambient residue and read it as scenery, which is LSN-026 in its natural habitat. Publishing to the `gke-labs` org is a permission the harness does not hold. | human | An unauthenticated manifest fetch returns 200 for all four `ghcr.io/gke-labs/kube-agents/<name>:v0.1.0` tags. Deliberately a REGISTRY read and not a workflow read: the L0 test already proves the workflow side, and proved it green throughout the entire period every one of these tags was unpullable, so re-reading workflows can never promote this row. Promotion needs a networked check, which puts it at L2/L3 rather than in `test_image_provenance.py`, whose hermeticity is worth keeping intact. |

| 2026-07-26 | **LSN-028** | Remote dev loop — a pure-allowlist egress policy denied the one destination it explicitly lists, on the first run of a suite that had been green for weeks | **closed** (mechanized) | The allow rule was `ipBlock: <allowed-server podIP>/32`. Dataplane V2 is Cilium, which resolves pod-to-pod traffic by **endpoint identity**; a CIDR selector names no identity, so the rule matched nothing and the destination fell through to the default deny. Calico honours the same rule, which is why the fixture had never been wrong before — and `ipBlock` is neither broken nor deprecated, it is simply the mechanism for addresses that have no endpoint identity, i.e. everything OUTSIDE the cluster. Measured, not inferred: same two pods, no policy ⇒ REACHABLE, `ipBlock <podIP>/32` ⇒ BLOCKED, `podSelector` ⇒ REACHABLE. Generalized: **an over-blocking allowlist fails SAFE, so the red line it produces points at the fixture rather than at the policy, and the cheap fix is to stop asserting the thing that broke** — which would have left a suite that only ever proves denial, on a suite whose entire point is that a pure allowlist admits what it lists ([[LSN-009]] arriving through a security failure instead of a refactor). `dev/tests/egress-enforcement.sh` §3/§4 now exercises each rule kind against the destination class it governs — `podSelector` in-cluster, `ipBlock` external — and the external arm is **SKIPPED, never passed** when the cluster has no internet egress at baseline. Portable rather than conditional: `podSelector` is honoured by Calico and Cilium alike, so there is no `if dataplane` branch to go stale. Run by `verify-phase5.sh` under `verify-phase7.sh`, line 1 of `L2-CHAIN.txt`. **Open lessons: 0 of 28.** |

The two implementations do not merely spell the flag differently, they **collide**: BSD `-f` is a format string, GNU `-f` reports FILESYSTEM status — and GNU writes its answer to **stdout**, not stderr, then exits non-zero. Measured on coreutils 9.7: 245 bytes over 6 lines, after which `\|\|` fires and the real epoch is appended as a suffix; the caller's comparison exits **rc 2**, which is not one of the three states P1 defines. `2>/dev/null` suppressed nothing because nothing went to stderr. Eleven lines below, `date -u -d … \|\| date -j -u -f …` was already GNU-first and correct — the file held both orderings and no rule. Generalized: **the `A \|\| B` portability idiom is only sound when the losing branch is silent, and where the flags COLLIDE the loser succeeds at something else and pollutes stdout** — so write the GNU form first, because GNU is the side whose collisions produce output. Second half of the lesson: a portability bug in a failure branch (P1's three `date -r` calls) is invisible to every green run, so running CI on Linux does not find it and only reading the text does. `check_platform_idioms_are_gnu_first` (L0-CHAIN) scans `dev/`, `hack/`, `k8s-operator/scripts/` for three colliding pairs in a 12-line window, through `_code_lines` so a comment cannot satisfy it ([[LSN-023]]), VACUOUS under 20 scripts, and recovers real file line numbers. The same substrate change exposed one more of the shape: `dev/test_capacity_preflight.py` scrubbed `PATH` to `…:/usr/bin:/bin`, which hides the real `gcloud` on macOS and **exposes** it on Debian — a hermetic no-network L0 test was making live authenticated GCP calls and printing the project's real CPU quota. Closed by an asserted post-condition on the scrubbed `PATH` that raises `AssertionError`, never `SkipTest` ([[LSN-021]]). Verified 13/13 L0 on macOS and 13/13 on Linux, 12/12 P1 tests on each, gate 14/14, mutation-tested (BSD-first revert ⇒ red at `dev/lib/preconditions.sh:98`). **Open lessons: 0 of 29.** |
| 2026-07-27 | **LSN-030** | Phase 8 MILESTONE improvement pass — **the pass's own mistake, and a recurrence of [[LSN-022]] two days after LSN-022 was closed** | **closed** (mechanized) | `git reset --hard origin/main` at the tail of a compound line, issued while still on the previous branch, destroyed seven finished-but-unstaged files; the same line's earlier `git checkout main` had already **aborted** on the dirty tree and said so, in output that had just been read. `reset --hard` does not abort. `git fsck --lost-found`, `git stash list` and the editor's local history all held nothing, because git had never been shown those bytes — recovery was a replay of every `Edit` call out of the session transcript (`applied=30 skipped=0`) plus two hand-repairs, which is luck with a good audit log rather than a recovery path. **The lesson is not "be careful", and it is not even the verb.** LSN-022 recorded this exact failure and mechanized it as `dev/mutate.sh` — **scoped to mutation tests**. The lesson generalized; the guard did not. So a correctly-closed lesson sat in `LESSONS.md` while the identical loss arrived through a different verb, in an ad-hoc shell line, nowhere near a mutation test — **[[LSN-019]] in a form its own check cannot see**, because `check_closed_lessons_are_executable` asks whether a mechanization exists and runs, never whether it **covers the act**. Generalized: scope a mechanization to the **act**, not to the **caller**, whenever the act is available everywhere. `dev/git-destructive-guard.py` is now a **`PreToolUse` hook on Bash** (`.claude/settings.json` — the repo's first hook, and the reason that file exists), refusing `reset --hard`, `checkout <path>`, `restore <path>`, `clean -f` and `stash drop\|clear` when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty, splitting on `;`/`&&`/`\|\|`/`\|`/newline because the incident's verb was the **third** segment of a line whose first had already failed, and leaving `checkout <branch>`, `switch`, `merge`, `rebase` and `pull` alone since each aborts on a dirty tree by itself. A clean tree refuses nothing. **Found by it:** the first command it ever blocked was the heredoc writing LSN-030's own entry, whose prose quotes the incident command — heredoc bodies are data and are now stripped before splitting, which is load-bearing for a guard staying switched on rather than deleted. `dev/test_git_destructive_guard.py`, **27 tests** on the L0 chain, each against a real throwaway repo, the first being the **literal** incident command, plus two that assert the **wiring** rather than the logic, because a guard nothing invokes is a comment — which is precisely how LSN-022 came back. **Open lessons: 0 of 30.** |

It failed on **thirteen of seventeen kinds**, every one returning `default-routine: no rule matched`: `delete SQLInstance`, `delete StorageBucket`, `delete BigQueryDataset`, `delete BigQueryTable`, `delete ComputeDisk`, `delete ComputeSnapshot`, `delete ContainerCluster`, `delete ContainerNodePool`, `delete DNSManagedZone` and four more were executable by an agent with **no human ever seeing them**, while `delete ConfigMap` — six lines away in the same file — gated. Generalization: before trusting a safety list, name the domain its author had in mind, then name one it excludes — **the tell is uniformity**, because when everything on a list shares a property the list is not about, the property is a boundary somebody drew without noticing. The diff has a second consumer: `when.fieldPaths` matching, where `PointerPrefixMatch` requires the **rule** to be the prefix. A rule naming one annotation inside a newly-created block is *longer* than the coarse op's path and cannot fire, so "ensure there is no annotations block, then set the whole block in one apply" writes a gated annotation without tripping the gate — silently. Found by two tests aimed elsewhere (`~1` escaping; loud truncation, which reported `Truncated=false` for 250 added labels because they were one op); neither was about granularity and neither said so. **Generalization:** a self-relative consumer cannot detect a systematic error, because a systematic error cancels — so the precision bar for a derived value belongs to whichever consumer compares it to something outside the process, even when that is not the reason the value exists. [[lsn-032]]'s geometry one level in. Mechanized by **`assertLeafOps`** + `TestDiffEmitsOnlyLeafOps` in `k8s-operator/internal/broker/execute/diff_test.go`, run on every PR by `k8s-operator-test.yml`: checkable on a single op with no reference to any other diff, asserted on both the add and remove arms, and mutation-tested by stubbing `subtreeOps` to return nothing. This is what a reviewer reads to understand choices the specs didn't dictate. **Phases 0–7 are in
[`archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md`](archive/LEDGER-phases-0-7.md);** below is Phase 8 and the two
phase-independent rows.
